threads.body: The Javadoc for this helper doesn’t mention that the exception event extractor is only applied when the exception-signal preview is configured to emit exceptions as logs. Without that, it reads like it also affects the normal span-exception event path, but `Experimental.setExceptionEventExtractor(...)` is only used when `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview` enables log emission.

replies.body: Addressed — updated the Javadoc on all the exception-event helpers to note that the extractor only takes effect when emitting exceptions as logs is enabled via the `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview` flag.

threads.body: This change introduces a new behavior under `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs`: Lambda invocation failures should now produce an exception log record with event name `faas.invocation.exception` (and the span should no longer have an exception event when running in `logs` mode). There doesn’t appear to be coverage for the `preview=logs` execution path in the AWS Lambda tests, so this could regress silently.

replies.body: Added coverage for the `preview=logs` path. `AbstractAwsLambdaTest.handlerTracedWithException` is now mode-aware: in default mode it asserts the span carries the exception event, and under `emitExceptionAsLogs()` it asserts no span exception event plus a `faas.invocation.exception` log record (Severity.ERROR) with the exception attributes. This runs via a new per-module `testExceptionSignalLogs` Gradle task (library + javaagent). A `FaasExceptionEventExtractorsTest` unit test in `instrumentation-api-incubator` covers the extractor directly as well.

threads.body: In `handlerTracedWithException()`, when `emitExceptionAsSpanEvents()` is false (e.g., `otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview=logs`), the test currently does not assert that the span has *no* exception event. This means a regression where exceptions are still recorded as span events in `logs` mode would not be caught. You can keep the test mode-aware while still asserting the absence by always calling `hasException(...)` with `null` when span events are disabled (this pattern is used elsewhere in the repo).

replies.body: Fixed. `handlerTracedWithException()` now always calls `span.hasException(emitExceptionAsSpanEvents() ? thrown : null)`, so default mode still asserts the exception event and logs mode explicitly asserts that no span exception event is present. I also normalized the AWS Lambda javaagent Test-task setup so the preview task inherits the same shared JVM args / `collectMetadata` configuration.

threads.body: [Testing] `assertInvocationExceptionLog()` only asserts that exception attributes are non-null. This can miss regressions where the wrong exception type/message gets logged (or values are truncated/overwritten) while still producing some attributes. Since this test deterministically throws `IllegalArgumentException("bad argument")`, it should assert the exact `exception.type` and `exception.message` values (keeping stacktrace as non-null).

replies.body: No code change needed. This comment was against an earlier version that only checked the exception attributes for non-null values; the current assertion uses `hasException(thrown)`, which verifies the deterministic `IllegalArgumentException("bad argument")` exception details while keeping the attribute count check.

threads.body: [API] `setFaasInvocationExceptionEventExtractor(...)` forces callers to pick a concrete response type just to satisfy generics. Accepting `InstrumenterBuilder<REQUEST, ?>` (like other exception-event helper methods) keeps the helper usable even when the builder is held in a wildcard-typed variable.
